text.p: Following are some of the main stories in Dutch newspapers today. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
HET FINANCIEELE DAGBLAD
- Dutch central bank DNB sells 300 tonnes of gold in 1996, raising Dfl 6.4 bn. (p1)
- Engineering consultancy Heidemij accepts with "great disappointment" rival DHV's decision not to merge. (p2)
- Amsterdam stock exchange gives wrong advice concerning end of year date for taxation of assets. (p2)
- Hutu delegation talks with brewer Heineken about their demand for closing Burundi plant. (p1)
- Profits growth of temp agency Randstad in second half of 1996 accelerates. (p3)
- Insurance, pension and property brokerage group Kamerbeek aims to boost annual turnover by Dfl 200 million to Dfl 800 million within two years. (p3)
- Royal Dutch Airlines/KLM considers appeal against the ruling in court case over controlling its partner Northwest Airlines. (p3)
- Union FNV thinks pay and conditions agreements should be a condition for company bourse listings. (p6)
DE VOLKSKRANT
- Dutch PTT (KPN) obtains majority stake in merger between internet providers Planet Internet and Videotex/World Access. (p2)
- Services and temp agency Goudsmit takes majority interest in rival Multiplan. (p2)
- KPN'S plans to move part of its staff from its headoffice in Groningen to The Hague worries the city and province of Groningen. (p3)
DE TELEGRAAF
- Dutch businesses fear economic effects from row between Indonesia and the Netherlands over Indonesia's Garuda airlines' pilot suspected of drug trafficking. (p1)
- Foreign public transport companies ready to take over Dutch public transport. (p7)
- Dutch-Norwegian Kvaerner Stolt Seaway Alliance among the six companies to compete for dismantling Shell's oil rig Brent Spar. (p23)
- Board chairman of Philips' Dutch activities is worried about technical knowledge of young people. (p23)
TROUW
- Marketing and communication bureau BBDO boosts 1996 results by a quarter. (p12)
ALGEMEEN DAGBLAD
- Van Lanschot Bankiers books 20 percent higher 1996 net. (p10)
- Plastic tubes maker Wavin 1996 net up by 60 percent to Dfl 21 million. (p11)
--Amsterdam newsdesk +31-20-504-5000
